html:
The sea battle on 2 September 31 BCE off Actium in western Greece, where Octavian's fleet under Agrippa defeated Mark Antony and Cleopatra. It left Octavian sole master of the Roman world.

Antony and Cleopatra had gathered their army and fleet in Greece to fight for Rome. Agrippa cut their supply lines by sea, and their camp on the gulf of Ambracia suffered hunger, disease and desertions. Antony decided to break out by sea. During the battle Cleopatra's squadron, carrying the treasury, sailed through the lines and away, and Antony followed with a few ships. The rest of his fleet gave up, and his army on land soon went over to Octavian.

A year later Octavian took Alexandria and both lovers killed themselves. Ptolemaic Egypt became a Roman province, and its grain began to feed Rome (see Egypt feeds Rome). Octavian founded a city, Nicopolis, "victory city", near the battle site. In 27 BCE he took the name Augustus (see Augustus becomes first emperor).
sum: The sea battle on 2 September 31 BCE off Actium in western Greece, where Octavian's fleet under Agrippa defeated Mark Antony and Cleopatra. It left Octavian sole master of the Roman world.
